record.paper_title: Resolving Open Problems on the Euler Sombor Index
record.context_brief: minimum Euler Sombor index for connected graphs with fixed order and number of pendent vertices
record.original_question: Let EUS(G) = sum over all edges v_i v_j in E(G) of sqrt(d_i^2 + d_j^2 + d_i d_j), where d_i and d_j are the degrees of the endpoints. For connected graphs G with a fixed order n, where order means the number of vertices, and a fixed number p of pendent vertices, where a pendent vertex is a vertex of degree 1, determine the minimum possible value of the Euler Sombor index EUS(G) and characterize all connected graphs that attain that minimum.

evidence.quote: The Euler Sombor index (EU S) of a graph G is defined as EU S(G) = Σ_{v_i v_j ∈ E(G)} sqrt(d_i^2 + d_j^2 + d_i d_j).
A vertex of degree one is called a pendant vertex, and an edge incident to a pendant vertex is called a pendant edge.

However, some key problems remain open: determining the maximum EU S index and characterizing the extremal graphs among connected graphs with fixed order and given girth; finding the minimum EU S index and identifying the extremal graphs when both the order and number of pendent vertices are specified; and characterizing the maximal chemical unicyclic graphs for the EU S index.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a simple graph $G=(V,E)$, let $d_i$ denote the degree of vertex $v_i$. Define the Euler Sombor index of $G$ by
$$\mathrm{EUS}(G)=\sum_{v_iv_j\in E(G)}\sqrt{d_i^2+d_j^2+d_id_j}.$$
A pendent vertex is a vertex of degree $1$. Fix integers $n\ge 2$ and $0\le p\le n-1$, and let $\mathcal{G}_{n,p}$ denote the class of all connected graphs on $n$ vertices having exactly $p$ pendent vertices.

Determine
$$\min\{\mathrm{EUS}(G):G\in\mathcal{G}_{n,p}\},$$
and characterize all graphs $G\in\mathcal{G}_{n,p}$ that attain this minimum.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work resolves the maximum Euler Sombor index problem for connected graphs with fixed order and fixed number of pendent vertices (extremal graph being a complete bipartite-type graph), but the minimum case—determining the smallest EUS value and characterizing all extremal graphs—remains open according to the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Resolving Open Problems on the Euler Sombor Index (arXiv HTML)
status_evidence.snippet: The paper resolves the maximum EUS for fixed order and pendant vertices (Theorem 2.7, extremal graphs K_{n,p}) but does not resolve the minimum case of this problem.
status_evidence.claim: The minimum Euler Sombor index for connected graphs with fixed order and a fixed number of pendent vertices is still open.

status_evidence.title: Euler-Sombor index and its congeners (PISRT)
status_evidence.snippet: Khanra and Das pose open problems on extremal EUS index for connected graphs with fixed order and given number of pendant vertices.
status_evidence.claim: The problem originates as an open problem and the minimum direction has not been settled.
